newsitem.title: YEMEN: Crowds cheer execution of Yemen schoolyard killer.
newsitem.headline: Crowds cheer execution of Yemen schoolyard killer.

text.p: Yemen publicly executed a man on Saturday who shot dead four children and two teachers, shooting him with a Kalashnikov in front of cheering crowds across from two schools where the killings took place.

A large crowd jammed into an empty plot by the schools and cheered during the execution of Mohammad Ahmad Misleh, 48, who was sentenced to death for opening fire with an assault rifle on hundreds of school children last Sunday.

Misleh arrived at the site in a security vehicle flanked by about 10 police officers. Wearing a light blue traditional robe, Misleh showed no sign of emotion as he was led to the location where he was to be killed.

Onlookers chanted and whistled as they formed a circle around the area, while others scrambled onto the roofs of houses to gain a better view in the middle class residential suburb of Asbahi, about seven km (four miles) south of the city centre.
Interior Minister Hussein Mohammad Arab and other senior officials also attended the execution and were greeted with loud cheers when they arrived.
Misleh was forced to lie down with his face to the ground and was executed with five shots by a single sharpshooter.
As the shots rang out, crowds yelled "Allahu akbar" (God is greatest) and "long live justice" before breaking into thunderous applause.
After the execution, the crowds pushed towards the site of the execution to get a close look at the body.
Witnesses said it was the first public execution in decades, and many said it was the only one they could remember.

Yemen's supreme court on Thursday approved the death sentence ruling of a Yemeni appeals court, but overturned an order that Misleh's body should also be nailed on a cross for three days near the site of the murders.

Misleh opened fire on hundreds of children lined up in the yards of the neighbouring schools before morning classes. He killed a headmistress, a teacher and four children. Eleven children were injured, four seriously.
Misleh's claim that the shooting spree was an attempt to avenge the alleged rape of his daughter and the kidnappings of his daughter and son was rejected by the appeals court.
President Ali Abdullah Saleh ratified the death sentence on Friday night, giving the final approval for the execution, an official told Reuters.
